equipment.description: Submersible or vertical turbine pump for drawing water from natural sources.
Slow-speed mixer used to gently agitate water to promote particle agglomeration.
High-speed mixer for rapid dispersion of coagulants into raw water.
Rotating rake and drive assembly used to collect sludge in circular or rectangular clarifiers.
Centrifugal or positive displacement pump for returning activated sludge to the aeration basin.
Heavy-duty pump for transferring thickened sludge to digesters or dewatering equipment.
Centrifugal or rotary lobe blower providing air for biological treatment processes.
Mechanical device that agitates the water surface to dissolve oxygen.
Precision metering pump for injecting exact volumes of chemicals like chlorine or coagulants.
Pump ideal for handling high-viscosity or abrasive sludges.
High-speed rotating equipment used for sludge thickening and dewatering.
High-pressure pump designed to feed sludge into a filter press.
Hardened pump specifically designed to handle highly abrasive grit mixtures.
Electrical device that produces ozone gas for advanced water disinfection.
System utilizing ultraviolet lamps to inactivate pathogens in treated water.
On-site generator producing sodium hypochlorite from salt and electricity.
Mixer installed underwater in anoxic or anaerobic zones to maintain suspension.
Rotating screen for continuous removal of fine solids from influent wastewater.
Automated screen with rakes for removing large debris from the influent channel.
Helical screw used to transport screenings, grit, or dewatered sludge.
Continuous dewatering machine squeezing sludge between moving porous belts.
Positive displacement blower commonly used for filter backwashing or aeration.
Compressor providing instrument or utility air for pneumatic valves and controls.
Standard AC induction motor used as the primary driver for pumps and blowers.
Controller adjusting motor speed for energy-efficient pump and blower operation.
Centralized assembly of motor starters, fuses, and breakers.
Backup power generator to ensure continuous operation during grid outages.
Compact settling tank using inclined plates to increase settling area.
Tank where microscopic air bubbles attach to suspended solids, floating them to the surface.
Open basin using layers of sand and anthracite to filter out fine particles.
Enclosed vessel containing filter media, operating under pressure.
System of semi-permeable membranes using high pressure to remove dissolved salts.
Membrane system separating macromolecules and suspended solids from water.
Combination of a biological treatment process and membrane filtration.
Large sealed tank where microorganisms break down sludge in the absence of oxygen.
Open or closed tank where microorganisms break down sludge in the presence of oxygen.
Corrosion-resistant tank (e.g., FRP or HDPE) for storing treatment chemicals.
Vessel used to absorb pressure transients (water hammer) in large pumping systems.
Large reservoir for storing treated water before distribution and ensuring chlorine contact time.
Basin designed to slow flow velocity, allowing heavy grit to settle out.
Fixed hydraulic structure used to measure flow rates in open channels.
Submerged device that releases fine air bubbles into an aeration basin.
In-line pipe section with internal baffles to mix chemicals without moving parts.
Common valve in water works for isolation and coarse flow control.
Robust isolation valve used in distribution networks and main headers.
Valve preventing backflow, commonly installed on pump discharges.
Valve designed to automatically release accumulated air pockets from pipelines.
Valve that automatically reduces higher inlet pressure to a steady lower downstream pressure.
Flow meter using a magnetic field to measure the velocity of conductive fluids.
Non-contact sensor using sound waves to measure liquid level in tanks or wet wells.
Online instrument continuously monitoring the acidity or alkalinity of the water.
Instrument measuring water clarity by passing a light beam through the sample.
Monitor ensuring adequate disinfection levels by measuring free or total chlorine.
Device measuring fluid pressure in pipes or vessels and transmitting an electronic signal.
